skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Generate and transform videos through the inference.sh belt CLI using hosted models for text, images, avatars, editing, sound effects, merging, and upscaling.
skill.summary: Create AI video workflows with model selection guidance and practical belt CLI examples.
skill.author: skillssh

security_audit.summary: Markdown formatting caused most command findings, and ordinary links or placeholder URLs caused most network findings. Two low-risk URLs remain confirmed, while contextual review found medium risks from unpinned installations and external media processing.

remediation.issue: Installation commands and the external install guide use mutable upstream references.
remediation.suggestion: Pin every recommended skill and installation guide to reviewed versions or immutable commit hashes.

remediation.issue: Examples can send user media URLs to hosted inference providers.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy warning and require users to confirm provider terms before submitting sensitive or private media.

remediation.issue: The documentation embeds a remote image that can load during rendering.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the image with the skill or use a marketplace-hosted asset with defined retention and access controls.

content.user_title: Create AI Videos with Multiple Models
content.value_statement: Choosing and invoking video models can be complex. This skill provides model guidance and belt CLI examples for generation, animation, editing, lipsync, sound, and upscaling.
actual_capabilities: Selects documented models for text-to-video and image-to-video tasks.
Provides belt CLI examples for Veo, Grok, Seedance, HappyHorse, Wan, and related models.
Shows avatar animation and lipsync workflows using portrait and audio URLs.
Demonstrates natural-language video editing and reference-guided generation.
Covers video upscaling, foley sound generation, and clip merging.
limitations: Requires the external belt CLI, an inference.sh account, and network access.
Generated media quality, duration, resolution, and audio support vary by model.
Media URLs may be processed by external providers under their own policies.
The skill provides command guidance but does not verify model availability, pricing, or output rights.

use_cases.title: Create Campaign Clips
use_cases.description: Generate short product or campaign videos from written scene descriptions and optional reference images.

use_cases.title: Prototype Motion Concepts
use_cases.description: Compare video models and animate concept art before committing to a production workflow.

use_cases.title: Build Media Pipelines
use_cases.description: Combine generation, editing, sound effects, upscaling, and merging through repeatable CLI steps.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Basic Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a video of [subject] performing [action] in [setting]. Recommend a suitable model and prepare the belt command.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a simple text-to-video request.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Still Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate the image at [image URL]. Add [camera movement] and [subject motion]. Choose an image-to-video model and prepare the command.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn a supplied image into a short moving clip.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Talking Avatar
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a talking avatar from [portrait URL] and [audio URL]. Compare suitable lipsync models, then prepare the selected belt command.
prompt_templates.scenario: Synchronize a portrait with recorded speech.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Step Video Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a workflow for [goal] using [inputs]. Include generation, editing, audio, upscaling, and merging where useful. Prepare ordered belt commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Build an advanced media pipeline with several hosted applications.

output_examples.input: Create a five-second sunset beach video with visible waves.
output_examples.output: Recommended model: Grok Imagine Video. The prepared request uses a five-second duration and a concise sunset beach prompt.

output_examples.input: Animate a portrait with narration and realistic mouth movement.
output: Recommended workflow: use OmniHuman for broader avatar animation or PixVerse for focused lipsync.
Required inputs: a public portrait URL and a public audio URL.
Privacy note: confirm that both files may be processed by an external provider.

output_examples.input: Improve a silent low-resolution clip and add environmental sound.
output: First add described sound effects with HunyuanVideo Foley.
Then upscale the processed clip with the Topaz video upscaler.
Review provider costs and output quality after each step.

best_practices: Choose a model based on input type, duration, resolution, audio needs, and expected cost.
Use media that you are authorized to upload, and review each provider's privacy terms.
Test short clips before running longer or higher-resolution jobs.
anti_patterns: Do not submit private media without understanding external processing and retention.
Do not assume every model accepts the same field names or output settings.
Do not install mutable remote skills without reviewing and pinning their source.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What is required before generating a video?
faq.answer: Install the belt CLI, authenticate with inference.sh, and ensure network access is available.

faq.question: Can this skill animate an existing image?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents image-to-video models that accept a media URL and optional motion instructions.

faq.question: Can it create talking avatars?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse examples for portrait animation and lipsync.

faq.question: Does the skill run models locally?
faq.answer: No local execution is documented. The belt commands invoke hosted inference applications.

faq.question: How should sensitive media be handled?
faq.answer: Avoid private inputs unless you have reviewed provider terms, retention rules, access controls, and consent requirements.
